business_scope.primary_industry_name: Chartering and Operation of Offshore Platform Support Ships

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Samoa International Companies (offshore regime under the Samoa International Companies Act 1988, as amended)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Common Law statutory foundations with indigenous custom land/chiefly overlays; offshore corporate law follows English statutory drafting precedents)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Samoa-China Agreement on the Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (entered into force 2019)
Samoa-New Zealand Double Taxation Agreement (2009, with avoidance of double taxation and fiscal evasion)
Samoa-Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations (PACER Plus, trade and investment facilitation; WTO accession 2012)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2007 (as amended by Act 2018); Companies Act 2001 (domestic); International Companies Act 1988 (as amended, notably the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2009); Financial Intelligence Unit Act 2007; Samoa International Companies (Amendment) Act 2018; beneficial ownership reporting obligations under the FIU AML/CFT Guidelines and International Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Orders made under the International Companies Act; AML/CFT Act s.21A and schedule of beneficial ownership information.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (to be obtained post-approval of name clearance)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Samoa International Companies Registry / Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Samoa is party to the Hague Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency and Register of Directors and Shareholders (notarized extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered Agent in Samoa (licensed under International Companies Act, Part VI)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization if destination jurisdiction is not party to Apostille (otherwise Hague Apostille)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association (duly executed sealed copy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered Agent on behalf of the company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille through Samoa Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade or Attorney General's Office (depending on document origin)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Bank and Commercial References for Ultimate Beneficial Owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank or recognized financial institution in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (recommended for high-risk jurisdictions) or Hague Apostille if applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport certified true copies of all Ultimate Beneficial Owners, Directors, and Authorized Signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing government authority (passport office); notarization by a licensed notary public in the country of issuance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as required by the receiving bank/registry

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence PPP screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the Samoa FIU's PEP list, OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and HM Treasury sanctions database; additional domestic screening against Samoa's Terrorism and Transnational Organized Crime Act lists; mandatory negative news and enforcement database checks; risk rating must be assigned and documented; enhanced scrutiny required for PEPs, close associates, and family members; for ISIC 5222 offshore vessel chartering, additional maritime sanctions checks applying OFAC's Maritime Advisory and any sectoral sanctions on oil/gas/marine services; source of wealth and source of charter funds must be verified where high-risk flags arise.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Companies Registry online name reservation portal (operated by the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour; online lodgment through the Registrar of International Companies / authorized registered agents)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in the Latin script, with any non-English name permitted if it is accompanied by a full English translation or transliteration acceptable to the Registrar; suffixes must comply with the International Companies Act 1988 s.10 and must include the words 'Limited' or 'Ltd' as the final word; Chinese-character names are permitted only as a parallel foreign-language name, provided that the English name is the primary registered name and the Chinese characters are transliterated or romanized in accordance with the Registrar's guidelines; misleading, deceptive, or names implying a connection with the Samoan Government, the United Nations, or any sovereign state are prohibited without ministerial consent.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Ocean-going Vessel Charter (where statutory license is not yet obtained)
Any token requiring prior ministerial approval from the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, the Central Bank of Samoa, or the Minister of Finance
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant (through a licensed registered agent) may file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar of International Companies within 30 days of the rejection notice; the appeal must state the grounds of objection and demonstrate compliance with the International Companies Act 1988 and any relevant sector licensing requirements; the Registrar must issue a decision within 14 business days; if refused, the applicant may further appeal to the Minister of Commerce, Industry and Labour within 21 days; judicial review before the Supreme Court of Samoa remains available as a final statutory remedy. A single re-application with an amended name is permitted without a formal appeal, subject to payment of the applicable filing fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are not permitted as the registered office; the registered agent must maintain a physical office in Samoa (International Companies Act 1988 s.111). However, the agent's physical address may serve as the company's registered office; the company's actual commercial operations and vessel chartering management may occur outside Samoa, but the registered agent must be able to accept legal process and maintain corporate records at the physical Samoan address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium (quantified at approximately 20% annually for maritime-scope International Companies, given that they attract enhanced AML/CFT scrutiny due to medium-risk classification and supplementary shipping-sector guidance; unannounced inspections are conducted by the Registrar of International Companies and the FIU's compliance supervision for registered agents; likelihood is higher for companies with non-resident managers, high-volume charter invoicing, or vessels flagged under flags-of-convenience where a material nexus to Samoa exists)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff; includes expedited processing surcharge if applicable

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered agent fee (first year, including registered office and compliance filings)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Samoa registered agent (private sector; prevailing market benchmark)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark range USD 450-600; established by licensed agent tariff, includes physical registered office and statutory records maintenance

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT UBO due diligence, PEP and sanctions screening (per entity)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered agent / compliance service provider (invoiced with agent fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for enhanced due diligence, including OFAC/UN/FIU screening and risk assessment of a medium-risk maritime charter entity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, apostille or consular legalization bundle for incorporation and UBO documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public, Samoa Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (Apostille) or consular post of destination jurisdiction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial fees plus public international law consular tariff; estimated for up to six documents and multiple UBOs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sector-specific pre-incorporation license consultation and application readiness (ISIC 5222 offshore support vessel charter)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Samoa Maritime Safety Administration / Marine Department, Ports and Maritime Division; agent's advisory fee for license roadmap
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory licensing consultation fee and market advisory benchmark for maritime charter licensing, including flagging considerations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Immediate-term regulatory compliance review of ISIC 5222 shell charter structure (no employees in Samoa, no in-country office)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for targeted substance-risk assessment memorandum and AML record-keeping policy set-up

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Miscellaneous filing communications and expedited handling (courier, bank apostille set)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended; Part II (Incorporation and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation), Part V (Shares and Shareholders), and Part VIII (Registered Office and Registered Agent)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: SIFA Form IC-1 (Application for Incorporation of an International Company) together with the notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association and Consents to Act of the first directors
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to an International Company; the constitution may provide for nominal or no-par-value shares and the authorized capital may be wholly unsubscribed at formation. No escrow account or capital deposit is required by the Registrar at incorporation, although subscription consideration must be recorded in the register of members and, if deferred, settled according to the terms of the share subscription.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that, the subscribers having executed the Memorandum and Articles of Association, the Company accepts subscription for its initial share capital, and the register of members be opened and maintained at the registered office. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office in Samoa be adopted as the office of the licensed registered agent in Apia, and the Registrar be notified. RESOLVED FURTHER that [Name] and [Name] be appointed founding Directors and [Name] Corporate Secretary, with authority to open bank accounts, execute chartering agreements, appoint auditors, and file all statutory maritime and environmental license applications. RESOLVED FURTHER that the Directors be authorized to complete vessel registration and Shipping Licence procedures and to take all ancillary steps.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) — Companies Registry, Name Reservation Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit SIFA Form IC-1(A) with up to three proposed corporate names ending in 'Limited', 'International Company' or an approved suffix. The proposed name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name. The name reservation fee is paid through the licensed Samoan registered agent, and the reservation is recorded once the search confirms availability.
required_dossiers: SIFA Form IC-1(A) — Application for Name Reservation
Licensed registered agent engagement letter
Certified passport copy of each subscriber
Certificate of identity for each proposed director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or subject to objection, resubmit with amended names within 7 business days; an approved reservation is generally held for 90 days and may be renewed for one further 90-day period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Offshore Registered Agent (Samoa) / Notary Public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association tailored to offshore marine chartering, with object clauses expressly covering the chartering, leasing, and operation of offshore supply and platform support vessels. Subscribers' execution pages must be notarized, and three certified sets of the constitutional documents are produced for filing with the Registrar.
required_dossiers: Name reservation certificate
Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
Certified subscriber signatures
Registered agent consent form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered agent or counsel identifies drafting defects, the constitution is amended and re-notarized before submission; if object clauses require revision, a supplemental memorandum of rectification is executed by the subscribers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application to Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File SIFA Form IC-1 (Application for Incorporation) together with the notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association, consents of the first directors, and the registered agent's certificate. Pay the statutory incorporation fee of USD 100 plus applicable stamp duties through the SIFA licensed agent portal, and retain the payment receipt as proof of submission.
required_dossiers: SIFA Form IC-1 — Application for Incorporation
Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consent to act as first directors
Registered agent certificate
Statutory filing fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition or enquiry, provide supplementary particulars or amended documents within 21 days; failure to cure the requisition may result in refusal, in which case a fresh application may be lodged without prejudice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, SIFA / Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon satisfactory examination of the filed documents, the Registrar registers the Memorandum and Articles of Association and issues the Certificate of Incorporation, which is conclusive evidence of the Company's formation. The Company commences juridical existence on the date stated on the Certificate, and the registered agent obtains certified copies for the corporate records.
required_dossiers: Registry-generated Certificate of Incorporation
Certified copy of filed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Opening pages of directors and shareholders registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate contains a clerical error in the corporate name or date, file a written request for corrected Certificate reissuance with the Registrar; corrected reissuance typically completes within 3 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolutions, Governance Records and Bank Mandates
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors / Licensed Registered Agent (Samoa)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or pass the written First Board Resolution adopting the initial share subscription, the registered office at the licensed agent's premises, and the appointment of directors, corporate secretary, and auditors. Adopt the statutory registers, prepare share certificates, and open the corporate bank account with Swift Wire and Maritime Escrow payment rails.
required_dossiers: Executed First Board Resolution (minutes)
Register of members and transfers
Register of directors and secretaries
Corporate bank account opening forms with KYC/CDD pack
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If quorum is challenged, reconvene with proper notice under the Articles of Association; if banking KYC is queried, supplement with the corporate certificate of good standing, beneficial ownership declaration, and confirming board mandate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Works, Transport and Infrastructure (MWTI) — Maritime Division; Samoa Ports Authority; Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (PUMA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Shipping Licence application under the Shipping Act 1998 for operation of the offshore supply vessel, submit the vessel tonnage and classification particulars, and register the vessel on the Samoa Ship Registry. Concurrently lodge the environmental registration with PUMA/MNRE and obtain the fire safety certificate for the Samoan registered office premises.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Vessel tonnage and load line certificates
Safety construction and MARPOL compliance certificates
EIA registration or decision notice from PUMA/MNRE
Fire safety certificate from Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Maritime Division requires survey or supplementary documentation, complete the deficiency list within 60 days; an adverse licensing decision may be appealed to the Minister of Works, Transport and Infrastructure within 14 days of the notice of decision.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Works, Transport and Infrastructure (MWTI) — Maritime Division; Samoa Ports Authority
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Shipping Licence for Commercial Offshore Supply Vessel Operations under the Shipping Act 1998 (Samoa), together with registration on the Samoa Ship Registry

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) — Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B — EIA Registration for vessel charter operations; Full EIA Report required if operations involve seabed works, port construction, or discharge in environmentally sensitive areas within Samoan waters
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: MARPOL 73/78 Annexes I–VI compliance: oily water discharge ≤15 ppm via approved oil-water separators; no sewage discharge within 3 nautical miles of the nearest land; zero garbage discharge into Samoan territorial waters; marine fuel sulfur content ≤0.50% m/m and NOx Tier II engine emission ratings; ballast water management per applicable Samoa and IMO standards

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA) for the registered office premises; structural load inspection and load line safety construction certificates from an MWTI-recognized classification society; occupational and workplace clearance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act 2006 (Samoa)

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue (Matagaluega o Tupe Mau a Samoa), online portal: Samoa Ministry for Revenue e-Services (https://www.revenue.gov.ws)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must apply to the Ministry for Revenue for a Tax Identification Number (TIN) by submitting TIN application forms (Form TIN-001) and, where applicable, VAGST registration forms (Form VR-001), together with the certified certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles of association, evidence of registered office and local agent in Samoa, passport copies of directors/ultimate beneficial owners, and proof of authority for foreign registration. VAGST registration becomes compulsory within 10 days of exceeding the WST 100,000 taxable turnover threshold; an International Company engaged exclusively in offshore business may apply for non-resident/offshore enterprise classification to be excluded from income tax and VAGST registration requirements.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa does not offer a check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election mechanism. An International Company may elect to surrender its international status and re-register as a domestic company under the Companies Act 2001, thereby becoming subject to ordinary Samoan income tax. No other entity classification election is available under Samoa's tax law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1992
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 (Samoan Tālā) in taxable supplies over any 12-month period
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time electronic invoicing, fiscal clearance, API-based reporting, or digital stamping regime is currently operational in Samoa. Taxpayers must retain manual or electronic invoices in a form acceptable to the Ministry for Revenue. Customs export declarations are processed through the ASYCUDA World system, which requires electronic manifest data; no additional e-invoicing clearance is imposed.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated export treatment applies to supplies of goods and services exported from Samoa, including the charter of sea-going vessels used in international or offshore trade, provided the charterer is a non-resident and the vessel is not consumed or used within Samoa. For offshore supply vessel leasing, the charter must be substantiated as employment exclusively in offshore support activities outside Samoan territorial waters, and consideration must be received in foreign currency.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent export zero-rating claims are subject to retrospective clawback of the zero rate, disallowance of associated input tax credits, assessment of underpaid VAGST with interest at the statutory rate, civil penalties of up to 150% of the avoided tax under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1992, and criminal prosecution with fines up to WST 20,000 and/or imprisonment for up to three years. The Ministry for Revenue may reopen assessments for up to eight years where fraud or wilful default is established.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), acting as the Exchange Control Authority under the Exchange Control Act 1976 and the Central Bank Act 1984, in coordination with the Ministry of Finance and the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) for offshore company related approvals.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) operates under a managed float, with current account convertibility generally liberalized subject to prior notification to an authorized dealer for transactions exceeding prescribed thresholds. Capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment injections, offshore loans, guarantees, and issuance of equity to non-residents, require exchange control approval or documented notification via the prescribed Central Bank of Samoa forms. Profit remittances by an International Company (IC) are permissible once the distributing entity demonstrates compliance with the Foreign Investment Act, provides audited financial statements or a solvency certificate, and obtains tax clearance; however, dividend remittances to non-residents attract enhanced review where the IC is tax-exempt and the underlying capital was sourced from related-party cross-border financing. Dividends and charter hire remittances are treated as current transfers and are not subject to capital gains withholding, but remissions require the bank to record the transaction under the CBS Foreign Exchange Reporting Framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Charter hire earned by the offshore supply vessel leasing entity is classified as invisible export earnings under the Exchange Control Act 1976. Such foreign currency proceeds must be repatriated to Samoa through an authorized dealer within 30 days of the contractual invoice due date where the vessel operates on cross-border voyages, and in all cases no later than 90 days from the date of invoice issuance. The statutory default is 100% mandatory surrender of collected foreign currency into WST at the prevailing authorized dealer rate, unless the Central Bank of Samoa has granted a Foreign Currency Account (FCA) facility permitting retention of proceeds for working capital, loan servicing, or vessel operating expenditure; any FCA retention is capped at the approved limit and subject to quarterly reporting. For vessels on bareboat charter to non-resident operators, the CBC Class statutory timeline is extended to 180 days but the full proceeds must be credited to a Samoan licensed bank account prior to any discretionary reinvestment or repayment of shareholder advances.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account, USD and WST dual-denomination Operational Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (BSP) Samoa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account, Foreign Currency Account (FCA) approved for USD charter hire retention

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low-to-Medium for operational collection purposes and Not Viable for capital injection or statutory escrow custody. Legal constraints: Samoa has no licensing framework for foreign electronic money institutions (EMIs), and the Central Bank of Samoa does not recognize offshore EMI licenses as equivalent to an authorized dealer status. Consequently, the WS International Company may use an offshore EMI (e.g., Airwallex, Currencycloud, or MultiPass) exclusively as a vetting and collection aggregation layer for charter hire paid by counterparties in restricted remittance corridors, provided all funds are swept within 48 hours into a CBS-licensed commercial bank account. The EMI cannot clear capital escrow obligations, cannot provide an FX hedging execution venue for CBS-reportable exposures, and must submit a no-objection letter from the FIU where aggregate monthly throughput exceeds USD 50,000 equivalent.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: At least one director of the WS International Company must attend a face-to-face KYC interview at the commercial bank's branch in Apia during onboarding for this Medium_Risk_Enhanced marine charter classification, unless a shareholding director already maintains a prominent banking relationship with that institution. Remote opening via video conference is permitted only where the company's licensed registered agent (offshore fiduciary) physically attests the identity of all directors and beneficial owners on a certified Schedule of Beneficial Ownership, and the bank's compliance officer approves an exception on a named-client basis; the default CBS-aligned policy, however, requires physical appearance for new ICs in the offshore maritime sector due to the heightened trade-based money laundering and sanctions exposure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Discretionary trust or nominee-arranged shareholding obscuring the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) of the International Company.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete certified trust deed or certified extract of the trust deed; UBO declaration on the Central Bank of Samoa prescribed form; registered agent incumbency certificate and license number; sworn source of wealth and source of funds statement for the settlor, protector, and beneficiary; passport copies and proof of residential address for each individual with 25% or greater economic interest; corporate chart/ownership cascade to the ultimate human being.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Maritime operations exposing the bank to sanctions risk through vessel flag, port call history, or charter counterparties listed on OFAC, UN, or EU sanctions registries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: International Maritime Organization (IMO) number and flag state registry certificate; full charter party agreement containing sanctions and anti-terrorism vetting clauses; prevailing sanctions screening reports generated against OFAC, UN, EU, and UK HM Treasury lists for all charterers, sub-charterers, and vessel managers; automatic identification system (AIS) voyage logs for the preceding twelve months; protection and indemnity (P&I) insurance certificate; clean bill of lading where cargo operations are involved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: High-volume cross-border wires to or from FATF grey-listed or high-risk jurisdictions that do not correspond to the stated vessel lease trade route.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution approving the specific wire instructions; underlying charter hire invoice and supporting service tickets; CBS AML/CFT questionnaire signed by the compliance officer of the counterparty bank in the high-risk jurisdiction; bank reference letter from the remitting bank; route manifest and voyage orders evidencing the commercial necessity of the payment corridor; confirmation that the countervalue was subject to the mandatory export proceeds surrender timeline.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Newly incorporated International Company with no audited financial statements, no operating history, and requests for immediate high-limit capital escrow funding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or reviewed pro-forma financial statements for the first two operating periods; board-approved business plan with vessel deployment schedule; charter LOI or signed term sheet with reputable charterer; proof of vessel acquisition or bareboat-in funding documents; capital call notice and subscription agreement; bank reference from the parent entity; statutory declarations from the registered agent confirming the IC has not previously been used for non-conforming activities.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant injection route: the shareholder or external financier initiates a SWIFT MT103 (or MT202/MT202 COV where the remittance is nested through a correspondent) to the commercial bank's nostro account, typically in USD via a New York correspondent or in AUD via a Sydney correspondent. The wire instruction must include in the reference field the Samoa International Company registration number, the purpose code corresponding to 'foreign direct investment – equity participation' or 'shareholder subordinated loan', and the FDI approval reference issued by the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL). The receiving bank will not credit the account until the following verification set has been delivered: certified copy of the FDI approval certificate; board resolution authorizing the capital injection and issuance of shares; source-of-funds confirmation with supporting bank statements; and, where the injection funds a capital escrow arrangement, the executed escrow agreement. Any single inward credit exceeding WST 100,000 equivalent automatically triggers CBS enhanced due diligence, beneficial ownership confirmation, and a three-day holding period for FIU screening prior to value-dating.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for operational disbursements such as port dues, bunker purchases, crew wages, insurance premiums, and management fees; (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit issued on SWIFT MT700 and amended via MT707 for procurement of bunker fuel, provisions, equipment, and vessel spares where documentary compliance under the charter party is required; (iii) documentary collections using SWIFT MT400/MT910 for freight and charter hire receipts against presentation of signed manifests and delivery certificates; (iv) Escrow Maritime verification rail, where the bank maintains a segregated USD escrow account and releases funds to the vessel operator only upon presentation of a digitally signed vessel service delivery certificate and the charterer's countersignature; all outbound USD wires require submission of the CBS Outbound Wire Declaration and will be routed via the bank's designated correspondent to avoid prohibited jurisdictions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forward Contract (USD/WST) available with maximum tenor of twelve months, restricted to underlying charter hire and fuel cost exposures, and must be booked through a CBS-authorized dealer with supporting exposure documentation

Offshore Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) on USD/WST permitted for non-resident hedging counterparties where the Samoan entity demonstrates an approved Foreign Currency Account for the related receivable

Cross-Currency Swap (USD/WST) executed with an authorized dealer, maturity-matched to the vessel leasing or charter agreement term, with mandatory quarterly mark-to-market reporting to the Central Bank of Samoa

Vanilla FX Option (USD/WST) permitted on a case-by-case basis for protection against adverse Tala depreciation, subject to premium flow through a CBS-licensed bank and a demonstrated trade-related underlying

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Company Return and Annual Renewal Fee Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March each year following the relevant reporting year; newly incorporated International Companies file their first Annual Return on 31 March of the year after incorporation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing and late payment incur prescribed SIFSA late-filing penalties; continued non-filing or non-payment of renewal fees for the regulatory grace period triggers a Gazette strike-off notice and administrative dissolution of the International Company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership / UBO Confirmation Statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SIFSA, filed through the licensed Samoa registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed simultaneously with the Annual Return by 31 March each year; must be updated within 14 days after any shareholding transfer or change in beneficial ownership.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Knowingly false UBO confirmation is a criminal offence attracting fines and director disqualification; persistent failure to file or update the UBO register supports administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Office and Registered Agent Annual Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SIFSA, submitted by the licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March, or within 30 days of any change in the registered agent or registered office address.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Loss of the registered agent without a replacement appointment triggers a 90-day notice procedure; if no new agent is appointed, the Registrar commences administrative strike-off proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is mandatorily imposed on a tax-exempt Samoa International Company. An independent audit may be required only if SIFSA orders an investigation, a member holding the statutory threshold requests an audit, or the company voluntarily elects audit for financing or charter counterparty purposes.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB is the preferred framework; relevant local GAAP is acceptable for internal statutory record-keeping. Financial statements are not required to be publicly filed for a tax-exempt International Company.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: An annual beneficial ownership confirmation must be delivered to SIFSA by 31 March, even if no shareholding transfer has occurred. Any shareholding transfer must be entered in the Register of Members and Register of Beneficial Owners within 14 days, and the annual confirmation must identify the current ultimate beneficial owner after each transfer.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Shareholders and Directors Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$600 – US$1,500 per annum for licensed Samoa registered agent, registered office, and Annual Return administration services.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not statutorily required; voluntary certified audit typically US$3,000 – US$6,000 depending on vessel charter transaction volume and record complexity.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax rate under Samoa's Income Tax Act 2012; effectively 0% for an International Company (IC) licensed under the International Companies Act 1987, which is statutorily exempt from income tax, capital gains tax, stamp duty, and business license taxes.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full statutory tax exemption for International Companies under s.99 of the International Companies Act 1987: exempt from all Samoan income taxes, no dividend or distribution withholding, no capital gains tax, no stamp duty on instruments, and no GST on offshore charter income. The only recurring government charge is the annual IC registration/government fee of approximately USD 200 paid to the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA). No tax holidays or preferential deductions beyond the absolute exemption apply.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No income tax return filing is required: tax-exempt International Companies are outside the Income Tax Act 2012 assessment net. The sole statutory filing is the IC Annual Return (Form 14) submitted to the Registrar of International Companies via the SIFA Companies Online e-Registry, supplemented by the Economic Substance Return (ESR-1) where a relevant activity such as vessel chartering is carried on.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, measured from the incorporation anniversary (IC Annual Return) or from the financial year end (ESR-1 return).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: IC Annual Return: within 30 days after each anniversary of incorporation, accompanied by payment of the annual government fee. ESR-1 Economic Substance Return: within 12 months of the financial year end. No provisional or quarterly CIT installments apply to an IC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full registered name of the International Company, registration number, date of incorporation, and jurisdiction of incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the exact name on the Certificate of Incorporation; no Samoan tax file number is required for tax-exempt IC status.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical registered office address in Samoa plus postal address; a post office box alone is insufficient.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The registered office is held at the licensed Samoan registered agent's premises; it is the legal seat for service of process and official notices.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, license number, and countersignature of the Samoan licensed registered agent confirming the company is in good standing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident IC must at all times maintain a licensed Samoan agent; loss of the agent terminates the company's good standing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Directors, Shareholders, and Share Capital
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names, addresses, nationalities, shareholdings, classes of shares, and director appointments; disclosure of nominee positions and proportionate shareholding.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Nominee directors from the agent's licensed corporate services pool are permissible; ultimate beneficial owners are recorded confidentially in the agent's AML register, not on the public return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Business Activity and Tax-Exempt Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of the IC's activities, confirmation that no business is conducted with Samoan residents, and declaration that no Samoan-source income arises.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Describe the activity as ISIC 5222 offshore platform supply vessel leasing; confirm charter negotiations, invoicing, and crew contracts are executed outside Samoa to preserve the exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Relevant activity classification (shipping or financing and leasing), place of effective management, number of Samoan employees, physical premises, annual Samoan operating expenditure, and core income-generating activities performed in Samoa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For offshore vessel chartering, document that vessel scheduling, chartering negotiation, crew procurement, maintenance, and invoicing decisions occur in Samoa; a nil-substance filing triggers automatic review and penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the IC Annual Return attracts a monthly late fee plus late payment interest on the annual government fee; continuing default triggers compulsory strike-off and deregistration by the Registrar, retroactively revoking the tax exemption. Late or inaccurate ESR-1 filing triggers escalating daily civil penalties, suspicion-based reclassification as a domestic taxable company, and personal liability of directors. Fines for breaching the International Companies Act 1987 may reach approximately WST 100,000 for bodies corporate, with separate fines leveled on registered agents.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% final withholding tax applies to dividends paid by a resident company under the Income Tax Act 2012, but dividends and other distributions paid by a licensed International Company to non-resident shareholders are statutorily exempt from all Samoan taxes and are remitted gross without any withholding obligation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Samoa's double tax treaty network is limited; the principal comprehensive agreement is the Australia-Samoa DTA signed on 19 October 2020 and in force from 2021. For a tax-exempt IC, DTA relief is typically unnecessary because the distribution is already untaxed in Samoa. Where treaty relief is nevertheless invoked for domestic-source payments, the beneficial owner must: (1) obtain a Tax Residence Certificate from its home jurisdiction, (2) submit the TRC together with a non-resident exemption/withholding declaration to the Samoan payer or paying agent, (3) evidence the shareholding threshold (e.g., at least 10% of voting power) or the substantive business presence required by the treaty, and (4) retain the underlying charter, share register, and TRC records for the statutory limitation period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory final withholding is 15% on interest and 15% on royalties sourced in Samoa. Under the Australia-Samoa DTA, interest is capped at 10% and royalties at 10% of the gross amount; industrial, commercial, or scientific equipment royalties may be further reduced where economic ownership is established. Because the Samoan IC is exempt and makes payments out of offshore charter receipts, payments to non-resident lenders or IP owners are generally outside the Samoan withholding net.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Samoa's Income Tax Act 2012 formally embeds the arm's length principle but prescribes no published Local File/Master File monetary threshold. The Samoan Revenue applies a de facto administrative review focus on cross-border related-party turnover of approximately WST 10 million or more per annum. A tax-exempt IC is not statutorily required to prepare transfer pricing documentation, but must maintain contemporaneous charter-hire rate cards, independent marine-charter benchmark reports, commercial contracts, and operating cost records at the registered agent's offices in Samoa to substantiate arm's length charter rates should the exemption be challenged.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (comparable uncontrolled price) preferred for vessel charter benchmarking
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Samoa International Companies (Economic Substance) Act 2019 and Economic Substance Regulations 2019 apply to any IC carrying on a relevant activity. Offshore supply vessel leasing falls within 'shipping' (the definition covers vessel chartering and hire); where bareboat leasing without crew or operational control is adopted, the activity may be characterized instead as 'financing and leasing'. Both classifications are designated relevant activities. The IC must therefore prove economic substance in Samoa: (1) management and control exercised in Samoa through board meetings and strategic charter decisions, (2) physical premises and a substantive registered office, (3) adequate Samoan employees proportionate to the chartering administrative workload, (4) minimum Samoan operating expenditure, and (5) performance of core income-generating activities in Samoa, namely vessel scheduling, charter negotiation, crew management, invoicing, and maintenance procurement. Compliance is documented in the annual ESR-1 return filed with SIFA; failure to satisfy the test triggers escalating penalties, forfeiture of tax-exempt status, and deregistration.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Sham Exploitation of IC Tax Exemption
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the IC as a tax-haven shell while the offshore supply vessel physically operates within Samoan waters or derives charter income from Samoan-resident platform operators; contemporaneous voyage logs, crew lists, and charter agreements falsely locating earnings outside Samoa to convert taxable Samoan-source shipping income into tax-exempt IC distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of all diverted charter profits at 25% corporate income tax plus a 20% late payment penalty, an evasion penalty of up to 200% of the tax avoided, and running interest; criminal prosecution before the Supreme Court of Samoa with fines up to approximately WST 200,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years under the Income Tax Act 2012.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed false annual returns or intentionally directed the sham are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax via anti-avoidance and veil-piercing orders; courts may impose personal asset freezes, travel bans restricting departure from Samoa, and custodial sentences on de facto controlling shareholders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The IC holds charter contracts and rental revenue but has no Samoan employees, no physical premises beyond the registered agent's address, and board and commercial management wholly conducted in Hong Kong or mainland China; filing a nil-substance ESR return or failing the mandated annual ESR notification deadline.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Escalating civil penalties under the Economic Substance Regulations, including a daily penalty for continuing non-compliance and cumulative fines approaching WST 130,000; sustained failure leads to suspension of the IC certificate, compulsory strike-off, retroactive revocation of tax-exempt status, and mandatory notification to the Samoan Revenue Authority for tax recovery.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face up to 2 years' disqualification from managing any Samoa-registered entity, personal financial penalties, and court-ordered winding-up with asset restitution to creditors; the registered agent may lawfully resign, and resigning agents must notify the Registrar, exposing the company to immediate deregistration risk.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT Violation in Maritime Charter Payment Flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting high-value Swift wire and escrow-maritime charter payments from undisclosed beneficial owners, structuring payments to evade existing sanctions flags on offshore platform operators, executing transactions without vessel-charter source documentation, or maintaining bearer or nominee share arrangements that conceal the beneficial owner of the leasing income stream.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Samoa's Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018 and AML/CFT Amendment Act 2018, money laundering offences expose a body corporate to fines up to approximately WST 1,000,000 and individuals to fines up to WST 100,000 or imprisonment up to 10 years, or both; the Financial Intelligence Unit may freeze the IC's Samoan bank accounts; the court may confiscate charter income equal to the full value of the laundered proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: AML obligations extend to directors and beneficial owners: approving charter payments without KYC/UBO verification, authorizing escrow splits designed to route cash into exempt channels, or concealing sanctions-linked counterparties triggers personal criminal liability, travel bans and departure restriction orders, asset freezing, and extradition coordination with the vessel's flag state.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Prohibited Local Trading and Derogation of IC Status
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Chartering platform-supply vessels to a Samoan domestic operator, conducting crew transfers, bunkering, provisioning, or harbor towage within Samoan territorial waters, or holding beneficial ownership of Samoan freehold real estate without converting the entity to a domestic company and obtaining the required maritime business license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The prohibited transaction is void and the IC loses its exempt character: the entire charter hire is assessed at 25% corporate income tax with back assessments covering up to 5 prior years, plus late payment penalties and interest; unlicensed domestic trade is an offense carrying fines of up to approximately WST 50,000 plus a daily continuing fine, and the Registrar may dissolve the IC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sanction local trading without converting the entity bear joint and several personal liability under Samoa's Companies Act 2001; courts may grant civil restitution orders, issue travel bans preventing directors from leaving Samoa until the assessed taxes are secured, and convict directors as principals for the IC's unlicensed maritime operations.
